content.content:
A ref-path entry in the detail panel's Content section shows the pointer cursor: while the pointer is over such an entry, the cursor is the pointing hand a browser shows over a link, not the text cursor the same characters would otherwise take. The entry is the repo-relative path squvoxyr presents as a visible link (squvoxyr), so its cursor is what the reader reads before committing to a press: the hand says the entry is something to point at and press, and it says so before the reader tries.

The cue appears on every ref-path entry, on every value of the path form and whatever that value's content type, because squvoxyr presents every such entry as a link and this decision follows the entry it presents rather than drawing a line of its own (squvoxyr). Nothing else in the panel gains the cue from this decision: the content type shown beside the paths names the type and is not a path and not an entry, so it does not show the cue (squvoxyr); the block, the section's label, the value's frame and the other sections gain nothing here; and a path mentioned anywhere else in the panel, inside the selected node's kind, content or rationale text, is not a ref-path entry and gains nothing from this decision.

The cue accompanies the press and is not the activation: showing the hand is not pressing the entry, and the entry's activation, its inputs and what they yield are rptlovpt's (rptlovpt), neither restated nor narrowed here. Nothing about what any input does or where it leads changes because the cursor changes; this decision adds no input, removes none, and offers no second way to press. Nor does the cue claim the keyboard: a hand cursor tells no reader that the entry can be reached from the keyboard, and this decision states nothing about keyboard reachability, focusability, focus order or what marks the entry while it has focus.

The cue is one property and stops there. This decision does not say which colour role the entry takes, whether it is underlined, what else the entry does under the pointer besides the cursor, what marks it while it has focus, or which element and which class vocabulary carry the cue: the colour role, the hover treatment, the focus outline and the entry vocabulary are each a separate commitment with its own check, and none of them is fixed, required, forbidden or implied here. It names no class, adds no style property, rule or stylesheet of its own, and places the cue in no file. It fixes the cue and the entries that show it; the carriers that draw the entry implement it, and it holds there whatever element and vocabulary they use.

The cue is not a measurement. Nothing here sizes, pads or extends an entry, and an entry is not asserted to be a target of any particular size. The canvas is outside this decision: the cursor over a node or an edge, and the size of any target drawn there, are not touched, restated or narrowed here, so the hit-target value recorded for those elements stands exactly as it is (wtywxppt).

A path that names no file is left where rptlovpt and squvoxyr left it: neither states how such a path is presented and this decision takes it up no further. Nothing here requires such an entry to show the pointer cursor or forbids it, and whether it does is settled where an entry's presentation is decided; the cue is stated as a fact about the entries that name a file, not as a rule over every path in the block.

Nothing here re-decides the entry. What a ref-path entry is, how it is presented as against the bare text of the block, and what activating it does are squvoxyr's and rptlovpt's (squvoxyr, rptlovpt); this decision neither withholds, replaces nor reorders an entry, moves none out of the section that shows it, and states no rule that resolves, normalizes or opens a path. It states one cue on an entry that already reads as a link, and the parts of that entry's presentation it does not name are settled where they are owned.
content.rationale:
squvoxyr committed a ref-path entry in the Content section to reading as a link and then stopped before the cue a reader meets first: it named the pointer cursor among the parts it did not decide, so as the panel stands a path entry that reads as a link still meets the pointer with the text cursor of the monospaced block around it, and a reader who points at one is told nothing until the press. Of the cues that index a link, a colour role, an underline, a cursor, a focus ring and a vocabulary, the cursor is the smallest and the most specific: it needs no colour role, no decoration, no extra element and no class name, it changes no text and no geometry, and it is the one cue that appears exactly where the reader is deciding whether to press. Spending one cue leaves the other four open for their own records, which is why this is its own unit rather than a clause inside the link decision.

wtywxppt records one hit-target value for the canvas elements it names, with a note that carries two things at once: pointer precision and keyboard reachability. A ref-path entry is a detail-panel entry, so the licence it draws from that record is the pointer-precision commitment in its note and rationale, an interactive element the pointer can reliably find and target, and the pointer cursor is that commitment made visible before the press. The keyboard half stays where it is: whether the entry is reachable from the keyboard, whether it takes focus and what marks it then are the entry's activation's and the focus record's, and the cue claims neither. Fixing the pointer cue and abstaining from the keyboard is not a narrowing of the prerequisite, since nothing here forbids or removes a keyboard route; it is one record taking one half of a note so that the other half is not claimed twice. Nor does the cue take wtywxppt's measurement: the recorded value is a hit-target floor for canvas elements, and the size of an entry's target is settled where the entry's geometry is drawn, so nothing here sizes, pads or extends the entry, and the cue is not asserted to be a target of any particular size.

Keeping the commitment to one cue is what lets the rest be decided. The colour role, the hover treatment, the focus outline and the entry vocabulary are stylesheet facts a reviewer can point at in the styles, so each is checkable on its own terms and belongs to the decision that owns it; settled here, they would either be restated by those records or contradicted by them, and the distinction between an entry that reads as a link, the cursor over it, and whatever else draws it would be lost. squvoxyr took the same care from the other side, naming the pointer cursor among the things it did not fix, so this decision answers exactly that one open question and leaves the others open. The path that names no file stays as open as squvoxyr left it: the cue is stated as a fact about the entries that name a file rather than as a rule over every path in the block, so an entry whose path does not resolve is spared a requirement it never earned and a prohibition it never chose.

Decidability at review time comes from the one thing this decision fixes: the cursor over a ref-path entry says that the entry is something to point at and press. A reviewer can name the refuting observation without inventing a rule, namely the pointer over such an entry drawing the text cursor the monospaced block would otherwise show, so that a reader who points at the entry gets no appearance signal until the press. The decision stays in words because it decides a cue rather than a rendering: the panel markup and the stylesheet are its carriers, gated where those artifacts are read, and this record is what they implement.
